name: qa_power_off
title: OS-POWER P2: the real off (VLPR, a polled wake): `power off` with no button held; the unit stays dark, a press boots it. The draw and the press are by hand

steps.say: OS-POWER P2, rows QA-GLB-117 and QA-GLB-103. Run qa_power (`power off dry` ends in a restart) FIRST. The unit is idle, NO BUTTON held. Have an inline USB power meter ready (M3) and, for the wake rows, a gate-checked build under test as a .ptf in Firmware/ (then run the wake again with no card). The register facts of the VLPR entry are confirmed on NXP's documents (spec 4.7) but this is their first run on a unit: if the unit restarts instead of staying dark, `power` after the boot names the step (`power: last off RESTARTED at step: ...`): send that line

steps.note: (a leftover overlay is put away: F8 is BACK on the Navigator, the keyboard (cancel, never accept: F1 accepts) and the choosers, OS-UXF-KEYS item 5)
Power is released and the hold is armed: the off is allowed (it answers ERR power: Power is down otherwise)

expect: power: off: the stages 0 to F, USB off, the lights out, then the VLPR off after Power is released
steps.note: QA-GLB-117: the stages run (about 0.4 s), USB goes (this console ends), the screen fades, the pads go out; the unit then goes dark and silent and stays so. A build without the VLPR off says `then a restart` here

steps.say: NOW, BY HAND (QA-GLB-117, M3): the unit is dark and silent and stays so; read the USB meter for a minute and write the figure down. A restart within a second means a clock or mode step failed (see the first SAY). Then PRESS Power for 1 s and RELEASE it (QA-GLB-103; the unit boots at the release while kWakeAfterRelease is true, the default): the unit boots (logo, project); `diag power` then says `power: last off ended by a press (the wake)`. Repeat with Power held for 10 s, and with a .ptf in Firmware/ and with no card: write down whether the bootloader reacts to a held button (it is up at the reset while kWakeAfterRelease is true). A brush of less than 30 ms must not boot the unit. PTA24 stays HIGH in the off (kOffCutsSdram is false in power_off.h): the draw is the figure with the SDRAM powered; a build with it true is the M3 comparison and must wake too. Then run qa_power_last: it reads the record of the shutdown and of the off
